The file gives a clear error for the signed-out case.

terms.meaning: The record that says who is signed in, kept for the current visit.
An error with a code and message that the app understands and can show to users.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: File setup and imports
sections.what: Describes the file and brings in the session lookup, the auth settings and the shared error type.
sections.why: The header states the file is the one place that answers who is asking.
sections.watch_out: The shared error type must be the same one the error handlers expect, or the message will not be translated correctly.

sections.name: currentUserId
sections.title: Optional user ID lookup
sections.what: Gives the signed-in user's ID, or nothing if no one is signed in.
sections.why: Lets pages decide what to show to visitors without forcing a sign-in.
sections.watch_out: Returning nothing must be handled by every caller that uses it.

sections.name: requireUserId
sections.title: Required user ID lookup
sections.what: Gives the signed-in user's ID, or throws an error asking the user to sign in.
sections.why: Likely reason: actions that must have a user stop early and tell the user to sign in.
sections.watch_out: The error text is user-facing, so changing it changes what visitors read.

summary: Gives server code a simple way to find out who is signed in, either as an ID or as a refusal.
purpose: Keeps the question of who is asking in one place, so every server action checks it the same way.
why: The header says everything that needs to know who is asking goes through this file. The reason is the single, consistent check it provides.
how: 1) Reads the current session. 2) Returns the user ID, or nothing if there is none. 3) The required version throws a not-signed-in error when there is no user.
inputs: The current server session, taken from the request.
outputs: A user ID, nothing, or an error with the code UNAUTHENTICATED and a message asking the user to sign in.
risks: Code that calls the optional version must handle nothing. The message is shown to users, so changing it changes what they see.
debug: If a user is unexpectedly asked to sign in, check the session is present and that the session holds a user ID. The ID must be set in the auth settings.
